Literal-probability conditional count kernel, version1
====================================================
This new package extends the examined generalized kernel to 0<pl<=pu<1,
including the seam p=1/2. It supplies conditional cell bounds only. It is
neither resource acquisition nor a full forest constructor/acceptor. Original
sources are preserved in original/ and SOURCE_TRANSFORM.json lists every
literal edit and their input/output hashes. The original source capsule and
all accepted artifacts are unchanged. Existing half-gap, moment-polytope and
sign-conditioned analytic premises remain explicit; this note only replaces
the left-half probability restriction and disables unused legacy APIs.

Probability and variance
------------------------
v(p)=p(1-p) is concave with sole stationary point1/2. Therefore its exact
range on[pl,pu] is
 vl=min(pl*(1-pl),pu*(1-pu)),
 vh=1/4 if pl<=1/2<=pu, otherwise max(pl*(1-pl),pu*(1-pu)).
The new pure exact helper checks rational ordered arguments in(0,1). Every
active use of endpoint-ordered vl/vh, scalar lower v, and interval v in the
examined source family now calls this helper. All untouched p,q endpoint
coefficients keep their original meanings. In particular no p->1-p, k->n-k,
beta->-beta or exchange of positive/negative resources occurs. The helper is
identical to the old variance pair on every original left-half interval.
It gives positive vl, so all retained positive interval divisions remain
valid, including a point or closed cell at the seam. Independent phase and
inward-sum half constants are unchanged.

Moment enclosures and floors
----------------------------
Because 0<vl<=v<=vh<=1/4, f(v)=v(1-2v) is nondecreasing on this domain.
The old lower/upper substitutions in the absolute-cubic numerator, rho strip,
defect lower base and normalized polygon remain valid with the corrected
range. Powers/root bounds for h=sqrt(v+s), the same-law coupled count
variance, Gaussian denominator and all phase H bounds follow by their old
positive interval operations. The normalized denominator is still positive
and piecewise affine in the same two cubic moments, so its vertex-ratio proof
is unchanged. The midpoint coefficient error for -q*m0+p*m1 is exactly
(p-mid)*(m0+m1); the old absolute error bound applies on either half.

For sigma=sqrt(10), the binary defect term is
 p(1-p)[(2sigma+6)p^2-(2sigma+4)p+sigma-1].
The bracket has positive leading coefficient and zero discriminant
4(10-sigma^2), so it is nonnegative throughout(0,1). Its sigma coefficient
p(1-p)(1-2p+2p^2)>0 licenses SIG_LO and the same Bernstein lower bound.
The full actual defect nonnegativity used when clamping a lower bound also
uses precisely the retained inward and coefficient gates. The sharp box and
sharp derivative routes retain all these gates. On nonnegative inward a,b
with a+b<1/2, a+b-a^2-b^2-ab increases in each coordinate; that proof is
independent of p. Failure of an optional coefficient gate continues to omit
only that bound, never to assert emptiness.

For the same sign-conditioned law, with literal positive-class probability p,
 beta=[v(1-2p)+s(2alpha-1)]/(v+s), mean=v/sqrt(v+s).
These algebraic identities have no left-half premise. Mean increases in v
and decreases in s, while beta and the s>0 alpha inversion are handled with
ordinary interval arithmetic. The acquired signed beta and mean are left
unchanged. Let tmin=1-2pu,tmax=1-2pl. If beta<=bh<tmin, the identity implies
s*(bh+1-2al)>=vl*(tmin-bh)>0. If beta>=bl>tmax, it implies
s*(2ah-1-bl)>=vl*(bl-tmax)>0. Thus the unchanged denominator/nonempty tests
and lower lambda=n*s floors are valid with the new vl, also when tmin,tmax
are negative. No sign choice is inferred from p itself.

For the rho floor, the retained outward moment bound gives
rho_lower*(v+s)^(3/2)<=v-2v^2+M*s, with M the maximum of the same bilinear
function of p,alpha over the box (attained at a rectangle corner). Convexity
of x^(3/2) gives A(v)<=[M-1.5*rho_lower*sqrt(v)]*s, where
A(v)=rho_lower*v^(3/2)-v+2v^2. At the new lower v0=vl and t<=sqrt(v0), the
computed A0=rho_lower*v0*t-v0+2v0^2 is a lower bound. If A0<=0 the optional
floor is skipped. Otherwise rho_lower*t>1-2v0 implies
A'(v0)>1/2+v0>0, and A''(v)>0, so A(v)>=A0 for all v>=v0. Its right-hand
coefficient is at most B=M-1.5*rho_lower*t. Therefore B<=0 contradicts A0>0;
otherwise s>=A0/B. This proves the existing rho-floor source after replacing
its lower v; it does not require v to increase with p.

Binomial probabilities, normals, phase and orientation
-----------------------------------------------------
For j=0..n the binomial mass has its maximum at j/n when that point lies
in the panel, otherwise at an endpoint; its minimum is at an endpoint.
The binomial closed CDF decreases on the whole (0,1), with derivative
-(n-k)*mass_k(p)/(1-p), including k=n where it is zero. Thus masses() needs
only the relaxed probability guard, not changed endpoints/counts. The
centered-binomial/Gaussian derivative formula already treats 1-2p as a signed
interval and remains valid with the corrected positive variance denominator.
For fixed p its maximum over lambda is still at a lambda endpoint because
the numerator k+u-np has constant sign as lambda varies.

Incoming j>k Cantelli/MGF terms retain their original direction. MGF factors
use positive q,p and the same common alpha maximization, independent of which
probability exceeds1/2. The incoming derivative gate differentiates in u;
its uniform Gaussian lower derivative now uses the true vl/vh. Its optional
failure and exponential compact-range omissions remain conservative. Every
quartic event minorant, common-moment expectation and Bernstein/vertex bound
remains unchanged. All normal/exponential compact-domain checks remain.

The actual central physical endpoints A=(p-a0)/h and B=(1-p-a1)/h must be
positive for the same acquired law; the existing sign_premise and its safe
upper caps are retained exactly. The sufficient complete nearest-count
conditions 1/4+Lambda/n<1, n*pl>Hminus and n*pu+Hplus<n also remain. The
eventual full forest must still cover every k=0..n and u in[-1/2,1/2]. It
must use acquired literal right-panel resources, not reflected left resources.

Disabled legacy and validation scope
------------------------------------
The unused exact_count_core_v5.cell immediately raises RuntimeError. Legacy
variance_geometry.validate immediately raises, disabling every dependent
geometry helper; only need() is used by the active kernel. The separate
finite_gaussian.panel API immediately raises. Their old bodies are preserved
for source comparison but are not part of this package's usable proof API.
This prevents use of their left-only allocation coefficient/sign and panel
indexing assumptions. Pure root/CDF helpers retain their old implementations.

Bounded checks exercise the seam/right intervals, old-domain exact dictionary
identity and selected full new cells. They do not supply resources, complete
trees or a new cutoff theorem. A future count certificate must freeze this
package and its independent review, bind actual same-law acquired contracts,
and independently replay every leaf in a complete forest.
